title: Diatom Red List Dynamics in Temporary Ponds: A Mediterranean to Alpine Perspective
content:
ABSTRACT

Temporary ponds are highly dynamic freshwater habitats that can support specialized and conservation-relevant biota, yet their role in hosting Red Listed diatom species remains poorly explored. This study aimed to assess the occurrence and distribution of Red Listed diatoms in temporary ponds from two contrasting environments: Mediterranean coastal ponds at Castelporziano (winter sampling) and alpine ponds at Gran Sasso (summer sampling). A total of 73 species were recorded at Castelporziano and 155 at Gran Sasso. In both sites, assemblages were dominated by Least Concern taxa (64.4% at Castelporziano; 60.0% at Gran Sasso). Strictly threatened species (CR, EN and VU) represented a limited fraction of the flora but were proportionally more frequent in Mediterranean ponds (6.85%) than in alpine ones (4.52%). Conversely, alpine ponds exhibited a higher proportion of Data Deficient and Non-Evaluated taxa (27.7% combined), indicating substantial assessment gaps. Although constrained by seasonal and spatial limitations, the results highlight the relevance of temporary ponds as habitats for diatoms of conservation concern. Mediterranean lowland ponds may act as refugial systems for threatened taxa, whereas alpine ponds combine high diversity with unresolved conservation status. These findings underscore the need for multiseasonal monitoring, improved taxonomic assessment and targeted conservation strategies.
